paragraphs: Friend, this passage is a whole lot of kings in a very short time, and it teaches one thing over and over. When people walk in the way of sin, it does not stay small. Nadab walked in the way of his father Jeroboam, and Baasha, Zimri and Omri walked in his ways too (1 Kings 15:26, 34; 16:19, 26). One man's sin kept getting handed down like a family recipe nobody should have ever baked.

Now look at Baasha. God says, "Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam…" (1 Kings 16:2). That's a man who got everything from God and still went back to the old road. I spent years in the dust of a junk drawer, so trust me, when somebody lifts you out, you do NOT roll back in! Every blessing you have is a reason to stay close to the One who gave it.

And then there's Ahab. The text says Ahab "did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him," and Hiel's sons were lost when Jericho was rebuilt "according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun" (1 Kings 16:30, 34). I think this one is heavy, friend. But look at what runs through the whole passage: what the LORD says happens, every single time (1 Kings 15:29; 16:12). So take His Word seriously today, and ask Him to keep your feet on His road.
